newsitem.title: UK: CLARKE RESISTS RATE RISE CALLS-FT.
newsitem.headline: CLARKE RESISTS RATE RISE CALLS-FT.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke has rejected calls by Treasury officials and the Bank of England to raise interest rates immediately, the Financial Times newspaper said on Monday.
It said the Bank of England's monthly inflation report, due to be published this week, would say that inflation was likely to overshoot its target on current interest rates.

Treasury officials and the Bank of England believe interest rates should be raised by at least a quarter of a percentage point from the current six percent immediately, the paper said, but Clarke had rejected their views.
It added that the government, which must hold a general election by May 22 at the latest, might call the poll in March or April before a rate rise was absolutely necessary.
The overnment aims to keep underlying inflation, which excludes mortgage costs, at or below 2.5 percent.
